summary: Communicates with Hokuyo serial or ethernet laser scanners and outputs scan measurements in polar or Cartesian coordinates for tracking workflows.
key_concepts: Connects to Hokuyo laser scanners over either serial or ethernet interfaces and outputs scan measurements as CHOP channels.
Scan output can be Polar coordinates for angle/distance or Cartesian coordinates for x/y positions with the scanner as origin.
Start Step and End Step restrict the measurement range and must match the supported range of the specific Hokuyo model.
Serial-only High Sensitivity and Motor Speed controls trade detection behavior against measurement error or multi-scanner interference.
Cartesian output is a documented direct source shape for Blob Track CHOP object detection workflows.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enable connection to the Hokuyo sensor

key_params.name: cartesiancoords
key_params.note: x/y position output with sensor at origin

common_gotchas: Only specific Hokuyo models were tested in-house even though the docs say serial and ethernet scanners generally work.
Windows firewall can block ethernet Hokuyo devices; each TouchDesigner install may need network permission.
Start and end steps are device-specific and must stay within the scanner's valid measurement range.
High Sensitivity can increase detection ability but also measurement error and is only available on serial devices.
Cartesian output is the preferred input shape for Blob Track CHOP workflows.
